start: I'm Tavi. My brother will ask here. If my name isn't on the page, he won't know where I went.
Then we can write it down.
So can the man I owe. He asks questions too.
Who gets to read the book?
The full list? Anyone asking after someone. A private note is different, but it has to stay with a person.

choices.label: Suggest a public name and agreed contact point.
lines: Protagonist
You could give a name and a place to ask, without writing down where you sleep.
Enna
Your brother could search the index directly. So could a stranger. Are you willing to put that much in the public book?
Tavi
Yes. Put Tavi, and the harbor clerk's desk as the contact point. I agree to that. No lodging address.
Enna
That is what I will record. A public contact entry, not permission to disclose anything else.

choices.label: Ask about initials and a sealed note with a willing keeper.
lines: Protagonist
Could the public page carry initials, with a sealed note kept for his brother?
Enna
I am willing to keep it. I would record the packet reference and sign for custody. If it moves to the Record House, its next keeper must sign the transfer.
Tavi
Use T in the public index. My brother has my permission to request the note. Nobody else. I agree to leave it with you, Enna.
Enna
I accept that responsibility. Finding the keeper may take longer than searching a public name. A sealed note is not a guarantee that a family finds each other.

choices.label: Support his choice to leave no personal entry.
lines: Protagonist
You do not owe the register a name. It is your decision.
Tavi
Then no personal entry. Count me with the people here, but do not write down my identity.
Enna
An anonymous headcount, then. You still have a place under the roof. Your brother will not be able to trace you through this page.
Tavi
I understand. That is what I want.

0: Nothing personal has been entered. We can discuss the options when you are ready.
1: Only the name and agreed contact point are public. That is still my decision.
2: I have accepted the sealed note. The public reference does not authorize anyone to open it.
3: No personal entry. Thank you for respecting that.

archive.0:
ANONYMOUS HEADCOUNT
No personal handling agreement was recorded. This source confirms a group, without an identifiable trail for a particular worker. It does not establish anyone's later fate.
archive.1:
AGREED PUBLIC CONTACT
Tavi authorized his name and the harbor clerk's desk as a contact point. No private lodging address was recorded. Relatives or strangers could use this index; this entry does not establish what happened to him later.
archive.2:
LIMITED PUBLIC REFERENCE
Initial T; deposited packet V17-Contact-T. Enna's custody receipt and a signed transfer to Record House keeper Mira survive with the reference. The note remains sealed; access is restricted to the brother named in the depositor's permission. The exhibit does not disclose its contents or establish his later fate.
archive.3:
ANONYMOUS HEADCOUNT
A worker explicitly declined a personal entry and still received shelter. The register confirms the group but cannot trace his individual route. His later whereabouts remain unknown.

journal.0:
REGISTER HANDLING
No personal agreement was completed. An anonymous headcount must not be treated as permission to publish a name.
journal.1:
REGISTER HANDLING
Tavi agreed to a public name and contact point. I did not give permission for his private address, and the register contains none.
journal.2:
REGISTER HANDLING
Tavi agreed to initials publicly and a sealed note for his brother. Enna explicitly accepted custody and a signed transfer obligation. The chain may be slower than a public index; privacy is not proof of a safe outcome.
journal.3:
REGISTER HANDLING
Tavi asked for no personal entry. The anonymous headcount still includes him. This source cannot establish his later fate.
